sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the phone life list
sections.what: Loads icons, the store, the card component and the life area type. No visible output from this part.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: SolarSystemMobileView (part 1)
sections.title: Reading data for each life area
sections.what: Reads the same stored data as the desktop map. For the academic, career, fitness and finance areas it works out the name, screen, icon, item count and health state.
sections.why: Likely reason: the phone view needs the same information as the desktop map, so the rules are copied rather than shared.
sections.watch_out: These rules are a copy of the desktop map rules, so a change in one file must be made in the other.

sections.name: SolarSystemMobileView (part 2)
sections.title: Creative rule, badge labels and card header
sections.what: Applies the creative area rule, defines the label and colour for each health state, and draws the card header with the user's initials, level and momentum percentage.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The creative rule checks for blocked projects in a list that only holds active projects, so the needs attention badge never appears for that area.

sections.name: SolarSystemMobileView (part 3)
sections.title: Tappable list of life areas
sections.what: Shows one row per enabled life area with its icon, name, item count and health badge. Tapping a row opens that area's screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: a list is easier to tap on small screens than a rotating map.
sections.watch_out: The tab names are not checked in this file, so a wrong name would send the user to the wrong place or nowhere.

summary: The phone version of the life map: a card titled System Orbital Telemetry with a tappable row for each enabled life area, showing its item count and health badge.
purpose: Shows the same life area information as the desktop map in a layout that suits small screens.
why: Likely reason: a rotating map is hard to use on a phone, so a list is shown instead.
how: The component reads the same stored data as the desktop map. For each enabled area it works out the name, screen, icon, item count and health state. It then draws a header with initials, level and momentum, and a row for each area with a badge. Tapping a row opens that area's screen.
inputs: Store data: profile, tasks, habits, assignments, internships, hackathons, projects, goals and notes, plus the navigation function. No props.
outputs: A list of life areas. Tapping a row changes the active tab. Nothing is saved.
risks: The health rules are copied from SolarSystemHero, so a change in one file must be made in the other. The creative rule can never show needs attention, the same bug as the desktop map.
debug: If a row shows the wrong state, compare its rule with the matching rule in SolarSystemHero. If a tap goes to the wrong screen, check the tab name for that area.
